api_added: llama_kv_cache::relocate_layer(...) extended with a new defer_retirement_for_research parameter (RESEARCH ONLY, unused by the validated real fix)
bool llama_kv_cache_retire_layer_backing(llama_memory_t, int32_t) -- C API wrapper, RESEARCH ONLY
void llama_context::invalidate_graph_cache() -- the actual fix's core mechanism
void llama_invalidate_graph_cache(llama_context *) -- C API wrapper, the actual fix's public entry point
backend_specificity: None -- every new function operates at the llama_context/llama_kv_cache level; no backend-specific (Vulkan/CUDA/CPU) code was added or touched.
ownership_complexity: Low for the validated fix (llama_invalidate_graph_cache is a single stateless call, no new persistent state). Moderate for the RESEARCH-ONLY deferred-retirement path (adds a std::unordered_map<int32_t, ggml_backend_buffer_t> pending_retirement to llama_kv_cache, with the disclosed sharp edge in failure_atomicity.json).
maintenance_risk: Low-to-moderate. llama_invalidate_graph_cache wraps a call (gf_res_prev->reset()) that llama_context ALREADY makes internally for the identical purpose (llama-context.cpp:808) -- it reuses an existing, actively-maintained code path rather than adding new logic, which should track upstream changes to that mechanism naturally. The relocate_layer/retire_layer_backing additions carry the same risk profile already disclosed in Phase 12D's maintenance.json (reads private llama_kv_cache internals under active upstream development).
upstreamability: The invalidate_graph_cache hook is plausibly upstreamable in spirit as a small, generic, already-precedented primitive (llama.cpp's own decode() function does the same reset for the same reason) -- exposing it publicly for external KV-cache mutators is a natural, minimal extension. relocate_layer/retire_layer_backing's upstreamability assessment is unchanged from Phase 12D (rebind mechanism plausible, deferred-retirement research escape hatch not upstream-ready given its disclosed sharp edge).
